## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the birth of Isa and on Maryam. None is used in this draft.
- The event is told at greater length in the draft for Isa (content/stories); this event draft stays inside its own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state.
- The caller in 19:24 (who called from beneath her) is read in more than one way in commentary; a scholar should decide whether the page names a reading. The words to be spoken to the people (19:26) are reported speech and nothing more.
- The chapters omit 3:43-44, 19:27-28 and 19:31-32; 19:27-28 refers by name to another figure, which this draft does not repeat.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The glad tidings to Maryam  (`#the-glad-tidings-to-maryam`)

Cited ayat: 3:42, 3:45-47, 19:16-21

> **3:42** وَإِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَىٰكِ وَطَهَّرَكِ وَٱصْطَفَىٰكِ عَلَىٰ نِسَآءِ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

> **3:45** إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنْهُ ٱسْمُهُ ٱلْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ وَجِيهًا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ وَمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
>
> **3:46** وَيُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًا وَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
>
> **3:47** قَالَتْ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ ٱللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ إِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ

> **19:16** وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مَرْيَمَ إِذِ ٱنتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَانًا شَرْقِيًّا
>
> **19:17** فَٱتَّخَذَتْ مِن دُونِهِمْ حِجَابًا فَأَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَيْهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا
>
> **19:18** قَالَتْ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مِنكَ إِن كُنتَ تَقِيًّا
>
> **19:19** قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَٰمًا زَكِيًّا
>
> **19:20** قَالَتْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَٰمٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌ وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّا
>
> **19:21** قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌ وَلِنَجْعَلَهُۥٓ ءَايَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَرَحْمَةً مِّنَّا وَكَانَ أَمْرًا مَّقْضِيًّا

### Claims

**c1** (3:42): The angels said: O Maryam, God has chosen you, purified you and chosen you over the women of the worlds.

**c2** (3:45-46): The angels said that God gives her glad tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, held in honour in this world and the next and among those brought near; he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and will be among the righteous.

**c3** (19:16-17): Maryam withdrew from her family to a place in the east and took a screen apart from them.

**c4** (19:17-18): God sent Our spirit to her; she said: I seek refuge in the Merciful from you, if you fear God.

**c5** (19:19): He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy.

**c6** (19:20-21, 3:47): She said: how can I have a boy when no human has touched me and I am not unchaste; he said that this is what her Lord said, that it is easy for Him, that He would make him a sign for people and a mercy from Him, and that it was a matter decreed.

**c7** (3:47): God says that He creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be", and it is.

### One-minute summary

The angels told Maryam that God had chosen her and gave her glad tidings of a word from Him, the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam [c1][c2]. She asked how she could have a boy when no human had touched her, and the answer was that her Lord said it is easy for Him [c6].

### Complete story

The angels said: O Maryam, God has chosen you, purified you and chosen you over the women of the worlds [c1]. They said that God gives her glad tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, held in honour in this world and the next and among those brought near [c2]. He will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and will be among the righteous [c2].

Maryam withdrew from her family to a place in the east and took a screen apart from them [c3]. God sent Our spirit to her; she said: I seek refuge in the Merciful from you, if you fear God [c4]. He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy [c5].

She said: how can I have a boy when no human has touched me and I am not unchaste [c6]. He said that this is what her Lord said, that it is easy for Him, that He would make him a sign for people and a mercy from Him, and that it was a matter decreed [c6]. God says that He creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be", and it is [c7].

### Deep study

The passages give the same answer in different words: in one it is easy for God, and in the other God creates what He wills [c6][c7]. The ayat name him the Messiah and Isa son of Maryam, and say his place is held in honour in this world and the next [c2]. The form in which the spirit came to her is not described in this draft [c4].

### Kids mode

The angels told Maryam that God had chosen her [c1]. They gave her glad tidings of a son called Isa, who would speak to people even in the cradle [c2]. Maryam asked how it could be, and the answer was that it is easy for God [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set the question of how beside the statement that God creates what He wills [c6][c7]. Another is that Maryam's first words to the spirit are words of refuge in the Merciful [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: when or where the glad tidings came, or how old Maryam was; the ayat say only that she withdrew to a place in the east.
- Not established: the form in which the spirit came to her; the ayah speaks of it and this draft does not describe it.
- Not established: how the glad tidings of 3:45 and the message of 19:19 relate in order; the passages are read as one event.
- Not established: how the pregnancy began beyond what the ayat state.

## 2. The birth and the sign  (`#the-birth-and-the-sign`)

Cited ayat: 19:22-26, 19:29-30, 19:33-34, 21:91, 23:50, 66:12

> **19:22** فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَٱنتَبَذَتْ بِهِۦ مَكَانًا قَصِيًّا
>
> **19:23** فَأَجَآءَهَا ٱلْمَخَاضُ إِلَىٰ جِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ قَالَتْ يَٰلَيْتَنِى مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَٰذَا وَكُنتُ نَسْيًا مَّنسِيًّا
>
> **19:24** فَنَادَىٰهَا مِن تَحْتِهَآ أَلَّا تَحْزَنِى قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا
>
> **19:25** وَهُزِّىٓ إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ تُسَٰقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا
>
> **19:26** فَكُلِى وَٱشْرَبِى وَقَرِّى عَيْنًا فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا فَقُولِىٓ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِنسِيًّا

> **19:29** فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ قَالُوا۟ كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَن كَانَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا
>
> **19:30** قَالَ إِنِّى عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ ءَاتَىٰنِىَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلَنِى نَبِيًّا

> **19:33** وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدتُّ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّا
>
> **19:34** ذَٰلِكَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ قَوْلَ ٱلْحَقِّ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ

> **21:91** وَٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهَا مِن رُّوحِنَا وَجَعَلْنَٰهَا وَٱبْنَهَآ ءَايَةً لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ

> **23:50** وَجَعَلْنَا ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُۥٓ ءَايَةً وَءَاوَيْنَٰهُمَآ إِلَىٰ رَبْوَةٍ ذَاتِ قَرَارٍ وَمَعِينٍ

> **66:12** وَمَرْيَمَ ٱبْنَتَ عِمْرَٰنَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِنَا وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِمَٰتِ رَبِّهَا وَكُتُبِهِۦ وَكَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْقَٰنِتِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (19:22): She conceived him and withdrew with him to a place far away.

**c2** (19:23): The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree; she said she wished she had died before this and been forgotten.

**c3** (19:24-26): She was called from beneath her: do not grieve, your Lord has placed a stream beneath you; shake the trunk of the palm toward you and fresh ripe dates will fall; eat, drink and be content.

**c4** (19:26): She was told that if she saw any human, she should say that she had vowed a fast to the Merciful and would not speak to any person that day.

**c5** (19:29-30): She pointed to him; they asked how they could speak to one in the cradle, a child; he said: I am a servant of God, He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.

**c6** (19:33-34): He said that peace was on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive; this is Isa son of Maryam, a word of truth about which they doubt.

**c7** (21:91, 23:50, 66:12): God made Maryam, who guarded her chastity, and her son a sign for the worlds; He breathed into her of Our spirit and sheltered them on elevated ground with a place for settlement and flowing water.

**c8** (66:12): Maryam, daughter of Imran, confirmed the words of her Lord and His books and was among the devout.

### One-minute summary

Maryam conceived and withdrew to a place far away, and the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree [c1][c2]. The child spoke from the cradle, saying he was a servant of God, and God made Maryam and her son a sign for the worlds [c5][c7].

### Complete story

She conceived him and withdrew with him to a place far away [c1]. The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree; she said she wished she had died before this and been forgotten [c2].

She was called from beneath her: do not grieve, your Lord has placed a stream beneath you; shake the trunk of the palm toward you and fresh ripe dates will fall; eat, drink and be content [c3]. She was told that if she saw any human, she should say that she had vowed a fast to the Merciful and would not speak to any person that day [c4].

She pointed to him; they asked how they could speak to one in the cradle, a child; he said: I am a servant of God, He has given me the Book and made me a prophet [c5]. He said that peace was on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive; this is Isa son of Maryam, a word of truth about which they doubt [c6].

God made Maryam, who guarded her chastity, and her son a sign for the worlds; He breathed into her of Our spirit and sheltered them on elevated ground with a place for settlement and flowing water [c7]. Maryam, daughter of Imran, confirmed the words of her Lord and His books and was among the devout [c8].

### Deep study

The ayat on the cradle speech are partly reported by the child and partly closed by the ayah calling him Isa son of Maryam and a word of truth [c5][c6]. The other passages describe Maryam and her son as a sign and speak of her as one who guarded her chastity, confirmed God's words and was among the devout [c7][c8]. The ayat do not say who called her from beneath her [c3].

### Kids mode

When Isa was born, Maryam was told to eat and drink and not to be sad [c3]. She pointed to the baby, and he spoke from the cradle and said he was a servant of God [c5]. God made Maryam and her son a sign for all the worlds [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the account sets her distress beside the words do not grieve [c2][c3]. Another is that the passages call Maryam devout and her son a sign for the worlds [c7][c8].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where the place far away was, how long Maryam stayed there, or who was with her.
- Not established: who called to her from beneath her; the Arabic can be read as a person or as the one under her.
- Not established: how the people reacted beyond the words the ayat record, or how long after the birth they came.
- Not established: the date or the day of the birth.
